GOAL: read the five proposals and the frozen evidence bundles, then place them under rank-2026-10-v1.
READ: all five IDEA blocks (l1pdo-rq, DEMARGIN-L1-CURV, pmi-geomargin-l1-rq, BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ, GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ) and the five bundles (e10be3a2caf57e91, aa31432fc3e0b58b, 27b5ac51b79ed630, 2a311217eab4a282, 5dee08eef77d0f88). All five bundles share E4-E11; only E12/E13 and some E10 contents differ.
OBSERVED (shared evidence, decisive): [E6] width-20 beam survival on 57,439 test rows - l1_br (pure hyperbolic level 1) recall@10 0.04671 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363; [E7] teacher-forced NLL - l1_br T4 NLL 9.03 vs euclid 1.23; [E8] first-level capacity ceiling - canonical pairs sharing a K=256 cluster only 0.0822 (negatives 0.0129), K=64 0.1547, K=16 0.3106; [E11] existing baseline same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067; [E5] successor entropy is strongly structured (top-1 mass 0.4375 low-entropy quintile vs 0.0543 high, Spearman -0.973); [E9] train-only cohort-profile signal is real (positive shares successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871 negatives, profile overlap beats all ten negatives in 0.5898 of pairs); BEABLATE has an extra E10 (mean branch entropy 1.1081 nats, median branch degree 3).
REASONING: All five are the same mechanism family (level-1 Poincare distance minus a behaviour-demand offset, levels 2-3/loss/STE untouched), so placement turns on (a) whether the offset weight is derived in geodesic distance units, (b) whether the behaviour statistic is computed through the curved assignment (loop strength), (c) how stiff the curvature is, and (d) collapse risk against the tight level-1 capacity in [E8] and the weak prefix signal in [E11]. Measured curvature/weight derivations: DEMARGIN c=atanh(0.5)^2=0.3017 (RMS vector to ball norm 0.5), w = measured mean half-margin (distance units) but over all 256 codes with a 3w clamp that can exceed the local bisector margin; pmi c=(0.5/s)^2 (same construction) with w = 0.10 * mean min_k D_k, an explicit 10% cap; GEOMARGIN c=1 default, w = 0.1 * Dbar / rms(z) (10% cap) but z frozen from a pre-pass that never sees the moving encoder; BEABLATE c=0.25 with typical sqrt(c)||u||~0.23 (near-Euclidean) and lambda=1/72000 (one e-fold over the whole 72k-step budget) plus a chosen w=0.25; l1pdo c=1 and w = beta = 0.25 (the commitment weight), i.e. not a distance-scale quantity.
STILL OPEN: final ordering and the objection wording.

FINAL ANSWER (complete, one block).
RANK: pmi-geomargin-l1-rq | position=1 | reason=Only proposal whose offset weight is an explicit scale-relative cap (w = 0.10 * measured mean min_k geodesic distance, [E12] c = (rho/s)^2 built like DEMARGIN's derivation), which protects the very tight first-level capacity in [E8] (K=256 same-cluster share 0.0822) from the code collapse every risk list fears, and whose PMI-adjusted surplus answers the measured behavioural signal that is not popularity ([E9] profile overlap beats all ten negatives in 0.5898 of pairs); its weakness is a stale frozen surplus, not scope.
RANK: DEMARGIN-L1-CURV | position=2 | reason=Strongest closed geometry->behaviour->geometry loop (curved softmax defines the demand it then subtracts) and its weight w is measured directly in geodesic units ([E12] c=0.3017 puts an RMS vector at ball norm 0.5, mild, unlike the l1_br arm of [E6] whose recall fell to 0.0467), but w = mean half-margin over all 256 codes with a 3w clamp can exceed the local bisector margin and collapse level 1 against [E8], which one run cannot detect.
RANK: GEOMARGIN-L1-RQ | position=3 | reason=Well bounded (max margin = 10% of the typical level-1 geodesic coding distance) and behaviour-off is exactly baseline (zero-mean z), but z is frozen from a one-off pre-pass that never sees the moving encoder/codebook over 3000 epochs, and c=1 puts an RMS item at ball norm 0.762 (2-sigma 0.964) where artanh stiffens - the regime [E6]/[E7] measured as harmful (l1_br recall 0.0467, T4 NLL 9.03).
RANK: l1pdo-rq | position=4 | reason=It has the same closed curved-softmax loop as DEMARGIN, but its offset weight is the baseline commitment weight beta=0.25, not a distance-scale quantity, so the behaviour/geometry balance is arbitrary; at c=1 its maximum offset 0.25*ln3 = 0.274 is likely negligible against inflated geodesic distances, and its own rich-get-richer EMA loop is the failure mode [E11]'s weak 0.0907-vs-0.067 prefix signal gives no headroom for.
RANK: BEABLATE-CURVSCALE-RQ | position=5 | reason=Most likely no-op: c=0.25 gives a typical sqrt(c)||u|| ~ 0.23, essentially the Euclidean limit, so the curvature switch is nearly inert, lambda=1/72000 is one e-fold over the entire 72,000-step budget so demand stays near its init 1 for most of the run, and w=0.25 is a chosen rather than measured constant; [E6] shows Euclidean-level-1 arms sit at 0.0621-0.0623, below the 0.065 target.
OBJECTION: all five are near-identical variants of one mechanism, and the only direct hyperbolic level-1 test in the frozen evidence is negative ([E6] l1_br recall@10 0.04671 vs l1_br_euclid 0.06207; [E7] T4 NLL 9.03 vs 1.23), while the level-1 headroom the offset must exploit is small ([E8] K=256 same-cluster share 0.0822, [E11] same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 against a 0.067 permuted null), so a single run that lands anywhere in 0.055-0.065 cannot attribute the result to curvature, to the behaviour offset, or to seed noise.
